# Installing the tools {#sec-installation}

## No installation: BNG Playground

[BNG Playground](https://ruleworld.github.io/bngplayground/) runs BioNetGen in
a web browser. Paste any model from this book into its editor and click
**Run**. It is the quickest way to try a model, and it works on any computer.

## Visual Studio Code

1. Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com).
2. In the Extensions panel, search for **BioNetGen** and install it.
3. Open a `.bngl` file and click the run button in the editor toolbar. Results
   are written to a time-stamped folder and the main output (`.gdat`) opens in
   a plot viewer.

The extension needs Python and Perl. It installs PyBioNetGen, which contains
BioNetGen itself, when first used. macOS and Linux include Perl. On Windows,
install [Strawberry Perl](https://strawberryperl.com).

To keep results out of your working folders, set
`bngl.general.result_folder` in VS Code's settings to an absolute path, for
example a `BNG-results` folder in your project.

## Python

The book's Python code uses two BioNetGen packages and the standard scientific
packages:

- [bngsim](https://bngsim.readthedocs.io): fast ODE, stochastic, and
  network-free simulation of BioNetGen models, run in-process from Python.
- [PyBioNetGen](https://pybionetgen.readthedocs.io): supplies BioNetGen, which
  bngsim uses to turn a `.bngl` file into a reaction network.
- `numpy`, `pandas`, and `matplotlib` for analysis and plotting, and `jupyter`
  for notebooks.

Install them with

```bash
pip install bngsim bionetgen numpy pandas matplotlib jupyter
```

Every model and figure in the book runs through this route. BNG Playground and
the VS Code extension run most models, but they may not support every feature
used in later chapters, such as network-free simulation through bngsim. If a
model fails in one of them, run it from Python.

## The book's models and code

The models are in the book's repository on GitHub. Download it, either as a
ZIP file from the repository page or with git:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/RuleWorld/bionetgen-book.git
cd bionetgen-book
```

Paths such as `models/ch01/stat_step1_binding.bngl` in the book are relative
to this folder. Check the installation by running Python from the folder and
simulating the first model of @sec-reaction-networks:

```python
import bngsim
model = bngsim.Model.from_bngl("models/ch01/stat_step1_binding.bngl")
sim = bngsim.Simulator(model, method="ode")
model.reset()
result = sim.run(t_span=(0, 20), n_points=101)
print(result.observables["LR"][-1])   # about 0.989
```

The chapters also use a few helper functions, for example to display model
files and generated networks, from `scripts/bookutils.py`. Each chapter imports
them in a hidden cell at the start. To run a chapter's code yourself, start
Python in the repository folder and run

```python
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
from bookutils import *
```

## Reproducing the book

To reproduce every figure and number, create the environment used to build
the book, which also installs Quarto and Graphviz, the program that lays out
the contact maps and rule diagrams:

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate bionetgen-book
quarto render
```

Stochastic simulations in the book set their random seeds, so they give the
same results with the same software versions. This version of the book was
built with the following versions:

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sys, importlib.metadata as md
pkgs = ["bngsim", "bionetgen", "numpy", "pandas", "matplotlib"]
print("| package | version |\n|---|---|")
print(f"| Python | {sys.version.split()[0]} |")
for p in pkgs:
    print(f"| {p} | {md.version(p)} |")
```
